_comment: Canonical mutate scope for the crypto mutation gate (ADR 0045). The single source of truth for WHAT Stryker mutates, read by both web/stryker.config.mjs (the mutator) and scripts/mutation_meta_check.py (the guard that asserts something was in fact mutated) — two languages, neither able to parse the other's config, so a restated scope would drift the mutator and its guard apart. Paths are web-relative (Stryker's cwd = web/). An EXPLICIT file list, never a directory glob: ADR 0045 §3 curates a logic tier and excludes the wiring layer — a file goes in only when it is pure at FILE granularity, because Stryker mutates whole files. Measured, which is why the argon workers are absent — argon.worker.ts 0.00% (21/21 NoCoverage: no test ever instantiates the Worker) and argonWorker.ts 19.67% (worker-vs-fallback PATH survivors: the tests pin the crypto RESULT, byte-identical either way), against v1.ts's 97.76%. Both are execution placement, not crypto; scoring them together reports the misleading number §3 exists to prevent. TIER 2 (cr-0174, measured 2026-07-19, each file whole-file/--force): the pure crypto-logic ring in features/spaces/ — epochs.ts, grant.ts, inviteName.ts — each measures 100% and is ADDED. grant.ts has no own test (its 4 mutants are covered by grantDelivery/rotation/inviteName siblings) and stays in scope with no new test — the file-without-a-test edge decided by measurement. EXCLUDED as wiring/mixed at file granularity: scopes.ts (65%, every export is I/O — crypto inlined in async bodies, not exported pure), identityPins.ts (74%, retry arithmetic + parse guards; only safetyNumber is pure), tree.ts (74%, real pure gaps — the fnv1a bound + the ä/ö folding branch — drowned in contentApi wiring; the trim-regex/reserved-char paths ARE covered), deviceKeyWrap.ts (71%, IndexedDB/WebCrypto, does not import v1). TIER 2b (cr-0175, measured 2026-07-20): tree.ts's pure slug/naming logic — slugify + fnv1a + GERMAN_FOLDING — is now LIFTED into shared/naming.ts (its real home is features/memory/, NOT spaces/ — the earlier 'features/spaces/ ring' framing mis-filed it) and ADDED here; naming.ts measures 100%. The lift is behaviour-identical with ONE gate-surfaced simplification: the trim regex `/^-+|-+$/g` had redundant `+` quantifiers (the upstream non-alnum collapse guarantees single dashes, so `^-+`≡`^-`) — two equivalent mutants, dropped to `/^-|-$/g` (same output, surface gone). The lift closed the two measured assertion gaps: an exact-value fnv1a pin (with a sign-bit input, so the >>> 0 unsigned-mask mutant dies — an ordinary positive input leaves it alive) and the ä/ö GERMAN_FOLDING branches (the NFKD path Café/naïve never reaches them). Trap 5 of cr-0175 was wrong that the trim-regex mutants die — they were equivalent, now designed out. What STAYS excluded, measured not skipped: tree.ts's content-key crypto (openName/openContentKey/nodeContentKey) is round-trip-asserted in tree.test.ts → ~100%, so it confirms nothing (a KAT-pinned suite teaches little) — gate surface without signal; identityPins.ts (home features/account/, NOT spaces/) is closed measured-empty — safetyNumber is a one-line delegate already vector-pinned in identityPins.test.ts whose substance (fingerprint/deserializeIdentityPublic) is v1.ts = mutate[0], and its real survivor mass (the mutateAndSave retry bound + unsealPins guards) is entangled with vault/network I/O, not liftable as pure. scopes.ts + deviceKeyWrap.ts stay wiring. TIER 2c (cr-0177, measured 2026-07-20): two pure-but-untested web crypto modules KAT-pinned + ADDED. accountBirth.ts (the cold master-key birth, features/account/register/ — was 77%, no test; the produced material had no oracle) → 100% via a seeded-RNG + fixed-identity byte-KAT whose expected wraps are built with HARDCODED AAD literals ('master-key'/'identity-priv'), so a mutated source context disagrees (a roundtrip reusing the source const would be blind). Its three Argon KEKs (kekPasswordSecret/kekRecovery/deriveAuthKeypair) are MOCKED — real Argon is ~2.6s/buildAccount (3× @ 32MB), which Stryker pays per mutant → the resented CI tax §3 rejects; KEK byte-correctness is v1.conformance's job (v1 = mutate[0]), accountBirth's job is the WIRING, which the KAT pins. nodeMeta.ts (the wrappedMeta seal, features/memory/ — was 65%, no test; AAD 'node-meta' unpinned + the E3 best-effort fall-throughs unmeasured) → 100% via the AAD pinned two ways + the three {v:1} fall-throughs (falsy/catch/non-object — the non-object input is a JSON STRING, not a number, else {...42,v:1}≡{v:1} survives) + a short-circuit spy that kills the else-EQUIVALENT `if(!wrappedMeta)`→`if(false)` guard mutant: output alone can't tell the guard from its removal (falsy falls through to fromB64std→throw→catch→{v:1}), so the test pins the guard's PURPOSE — fromB64std is not called on a falsy blob. The guard is KEPT (a useful fast-path), the mutant killed by observation not simplification. PASSIVE ADD: capabilityTags.ts (features/tasks/, already 100% via an existing test) — pins the two protocol magic-ids '02f271ff'/'663157d8' shared with the backend registry. RECLASSIFIED as wiring, NOT gated (the plan-correcting finding — both were named as targets, both impure at file granularity): trustDevice.ts imports accountWrapsApi (network) + ./deviceKey (IndexedDB+WebCrypto) + withRefresh — same class as scopes.ts; its 'master-key' AAD is the same string accountBirth already pins. scopeRotationWorker.ts imports tasksApi/withRefresh/scopes/members/activeSpace — an async claim→rotate→complete network loop whose measured 100% is fully-mocked brittle green; §3's boundary is purity, not score.
